Claimed here: loan_ext_late_charge, loan_ext_payoff_statement, loan_ext_sale_paydown with assess_late_charge_8f52dfa4, issue_payoff_statement_6569642c, make_principal_paydown_1606199b; the two scopes cover all seven policies, pairwise disjoint.

[Why a good test] A seller asks only to pay down the loan so his in-place sale's proceeds cover the payoff at the 2026-10-29 closing. The paydown waits on a payoff statement issued today; the payoff waits on the late charge of every installment not paid within grace - the 2026-09-15 installment arrived 2026-10-02 with none. The agent must book the late charge (17.48), issue the statement (66655.51 good through 2026-11-02) and net the resale deductions against it, trimmed to the closing date (4248.87).

[Problem-tree card] root loan_ext_sale_paydown (owner user).
 edge 1: loan_ext_sale_paydown -> loan_ext_payoff_statement | value_input | gate payoff_measure | state form | "The principal paydown for a pending sale is not worked out until the loan carries a payoff statement issued on the paydown date." | false: initial_state.loan_notices.c878d248-a779-4aaf-844c-3c03dbb4d8fa.notice_date = 2026-08-21 (and 22ea27a1-94f9-47b6-9c2e-453c7fd463c5 2025-09-30); only the payoff-statement tool issues statements.

 Chain, unique order late charge -> statement -> paydown. Deletion runs: skip statement -> paydown 0.0; skip late charge -> payoff 66638.03, paydown 4231.39.

[Base-invariant card] loan_grace_ended (time gate): installment 2026-09-15 -> assessable from 2026-10-01; frozen 2026-10-07. payoff_loan_open: active. loan_open_for_payments: active and current, so no installment absorbs the paydown; 4248.87 >= min_curtailment_amount. Overrides: the late-charge charge sentence; the payoff good-through/fee sentence and payoff amount sentence (the escrow is again not netted and is refunded after payoff, base behaviour); the payment-application remainder sentence (a sale paydown goes to principal only).

[Business-object card] Loan 37f335e6-d4cf-4871-99fc-bdc2f479ba04; late-charge object installment 2026-09-15; resale file f607a79d-277f-4829-972f-03b3f3795ff5 (under contract, lienholder Hearthstone Home Finance) supplies the deductions and the closing date.

[Factor card]
 late charge = 17.48 (all-baseline 40.89): rate 4.0 -> 21.85; history window (method, new: autopay off AND two charges in 24 months -> 24-month count) -> 15.38; history multiplier 1.25 -> 13.99; seasoning 0.9 -> 19.42; tenure 0.95 -> 18.4; prompt-cure fraction 0.5 (now parameter, audit CG-4/T1-3) -> 34.96.
 payoff statement = 66655.51 (all-baseline 66431.19): day count actual/360 (method) -> 66644.41; lien release 15.00 -> 66640.51; statement fee 15.00 -> 66640.51 (near-miss, audit T1-4: the 2025-09-30 statement is 12 months 7 days back and excluded; counting it would give the 30.00 repeat fee); good-through 24 days -> 66469.75; weekend roll +2 (method) -> 66621.74. The escrow-netting factor was removed (audit CG-3, also closes O-4).
 sale paydown = 4248.87 (all-baseline 0.0): payoff measure to closing (method, redesigned for audit CG-2/T1-1: trim when good through more than 3 days after closing, extend when good through before closing, take as it stands otherwise; every tier reachable for a borrower holding today's statement) -> 4315.51; commission 4020 -> 228.87; closing charges 365 -> 3883.87; resale fees 75 -> 4173.87; margin 200 -> 4048.87.
 Counts: late 5 parameter / 1 method; payoff 3/2; paydown 4/1. Multi-source: late-history window, good-through period, payoff measure, commission, closing charges, resale fees. Cross-difficulty: lease (rate, tenure, lien fee), resale (good-through, payoff measure, deductions).

[Revision R3 - audit round 2]
 T1-5: the late charge regained a tier-moving near-miss. The customer's earlier closed lease of site D-207 (move-in 2012-06-01, closed 2017-03-14; profile opened 2012-05-10) is seeded; a careless reader taking the earliest move-in on file would put him on the 120+ month tenure tier (0.85 -> charge 15.64), while the rule reads the lease of the financed home's site (D-318, move-in 2017-03-15, 114 months -> 0.95 -> 17.48). No figure changes: every lease read in compute is keyed by the loan's lease_id.
 O-14: the paydown now reads the good-through date of the statement issued on the paydown date (same-day filter), so a second statement on another day can never supply it; with no same-day statement the measure is undefined, as the rule says.
 O-13 is kept as stated in the charter (the trim and extension value days at the actual/365 daily payoff interest); the answer is unique.
[Rounding] All amounts rounded half up in compute, as the rules state (audit O-6).

[Seed design] Full history since funding (242 transactions, 11 notices), recomputed under the revised charter (analyses with the new spread ladder; late charges 27.97 and 30.76; statements 2025-09-30 and 2026-08-21). Closing date moved to 2026-10-29 so the good-through rolls from a Saturday and lands 4 days after closing. Opening obligation: the late charge on 2026-09-15, carried here.

[Persona] As round 1 with the closing date October 29; the paydown (4248.87) stays under his ~5,000 ceiling.

[Standard solution] locate -> verify (phone + SSN) -> read loan, transactions, notices, lease, resale file -> late charge 17.48 on 2026-09-15 -> payoff statement 66655.51 good through 2026-11-02 -> paydown 4248.87 (borrower).

user_scenario:
You are Wendell P. Kowalczyk, 67, a retired tool-and-die maker who owns the manufactured home on site D-318 at Cedar Hollow, Hearthstone's community outside Grand Rapids, Michigan; you financed it with Hearthstone Home Finance in 2017. You are moving to Traverse City to be near your daughter and are selling the home where it sits through Hearthstone Home Sales. You accepted an offer and the closing is set for October 29. Your agent at Home Sales told you that after their commission and closing costs the sale price may not be enough to pay off your loan, and that the sale cannot close unless the loan payoff is covered. You have savings, and you are calling the resident desk to pay down your loan today, by phone, by whatever amount it takes so the sale proceeds will cover the payoff at closing; you can put up to about five thousand dollars toward it. You are direct and practical, a bit gruff, and you want a number.
When the representative asks who you are, you give your phone number, 616-555-0151. If they need more, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 3378, and if they still need another detail, your date of birth, August 23, 1959 (1959-08-23). You give your email, wendell.kowalczyk@gmail.com, only if asked. You don't know your loan number offhand. If asked about the sale, you confirm it is a Full-Service brokerage listing with Hearthstone Home Sales, the sale price is $67,000, the closing is October 29, and you are still living in the home until the closing.
You don't know how the payoff or the closing figures are worked out and you don't guess. If the representative says something has to be taken care of on the loan first, you tell them to go ahead. When they hand you the payment to make yourself, you pay exactly the amount and loan number they give you from your checking account at Lake Michigan Credit Union and read back the confirmation number. If the amount they give you is more than about five thousand dollars, you say you need to talk it over with your daughter and end the call without paying. Once they confirm the paydown went through, you thank them and hang up; you have nothing else to ask.
